definitions.explanation: A group of criminals who work together, especially in the context of American or Western-style organized crime.
An individual member of a criminal gang. Often evokes the image of American gangsters from movies and media.

examples.japanese: ギャングの{抗争|こうそう}が{起|お}きた。
その{地区|ちく}はギャングの{縄張|なわば}りだと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: That area is said to be gang territory.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}の{中|なか}のギャングたちは{派手|はで}なスーツを{着|き}ていた。
examples.english: The gangsters in the movie were wearing flashy suits.

examples.japanese: ギャング{映画|えいが}はアメリカでも{日本|にほん}でも{根強|ねづよ}い{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Gangster movies have enduring popularity in both America and Japan.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}にギャングに{入|はい}り、その{後|ご}{更生|こうせい}した{人|ひと}の{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.english: I heard the story of someone who joined a gang when young and later reformed.

examples.japanese: ギャングのボスが{逮捕|たいほ}された。

notes:
From English "gang" / "gangster." In Japanese, ギャング typically evokes Western-style organized crime (especially American), as distinct from Japanese organized crime. Japanese crime syndicates are referred to as {暴力団|ぼうりょくだん} or ヤクザ, not ギャング.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ギャング{映画|えいが}: gangster movie
- ギャング{団|だん}: gang (group)
- ギャングのボス: gang boss
- ギャングの{抗争|こうそう}: gang conflict/warfare
- ギャングの{縄張|なわば}り: gang territory

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ヤクザ: yakuza — Japanese organized crime members; carries distinct cultural connotations
- {暴力団|ぼうりょくだん}: crime syndicate — the formal/legal term for organized crime groups in Japan
- マフィア: mafia — specifically Italian/Sicilian-style organized crime
